key_assumptions.input: Starting free cash flow per share
key_assumptions.source: FY2025 cash from operations $4,277.1M minus ~$200M capital spending, divided by ~359M diluted shares (10-K FY2025)
FY2025 mid-cycle base; Q1 2026 revenue and operating income run above trend and are not inflated into starting cash flow
Mid-cycle owner cash; exit near current ~22x cash flow multiple

open_questions: First Marvin deep dive; no approved third-party sources in base IRR.
Entry band **$210–220** for ~15% base return is illustrative pending human price confirmation.
Confirm FY2025 capital spending line in 10-K cash flow statement for FCF tie-out.
thesis: CME Group is the world's largest listed derivatives marketplace: futures and options on interest rates, equity indexes, foreign exchange, energy, metals, and agricultural products, plus clearing, market data, and collateral services. **[Fact]** Customers pay transaction, clearing, and market-data fees; CME does not take directional market risk on customer positions. **[Fact]** FY2025 total revenues were **$6,520.6 million**, operating income **$4,229.5 million**, and net income **$4,072.2 million** (`investor-documents/sec-edgar/10-K_20260226_rpt20251231_acc0001156375_26_000009.htm`). **[Fact]** Q1 2026 revenues were **$1,880.1 million** with operating income **$1,309.7 million** and net income **$1,154.3 million** (`investor-documents/sec-edgar/10-Q_20260424_rpt20260331_acc0001156375_26_000020.htm`). Terry Duffy is Chairman and CEO.
why_market_wrong: There is no dated payoff or structural discount here. **[Inference]** Q1 2026 operating margin is far above a typical mid-cycle year because rates and volatility lifted interest-rate and equity-index volumes; the market may treat that run rate as permanent. **[Inference]** Our base return uses FY2025 owner cash per share (**$11.40**), not the Q1 2026 earnings pace. Return is franchise earnings power at price, not a mispricing signal with a known catalyst date.
